summary: OpenRouter must use free models only.
Ollama local endpoints and models are forbidden; cloud-only models must be used.
Do not log, echo, print, or reference raw values from .env.
widget remove button (cross) must be positioned in the top-right corner of the widget
add shades of grey themes (Grey (Warm), Shades of Grey, Grey (Cold))
add interface translations for Spanish, Portuguese, and Turkish
Click-outside listeners for UI elements (e.g., sidebars) must whitelist their corresponding toggle buttons to prevent premature closure and immediate collapse-and-reopen cycles.
Strategic and design documentation should be consolidated into a single, telegraphic reference (e.g., strategy.md) to optimize context injection for LLMs and avoid attention bottlenecks.

Unit test suites must mock active and actual method signatures. Regularly verify and maintain unit test integrity, especially after major architectural or documentation changes where method signatures might drift.
Scraper-backed ingestion must not be labeled as official API ingestion; clearly distinguish between unofficial/experimental sources and official API integrations in connectors.
While migration approval is blocked, connector parsing, policy metadata, and persistence wiring must be kept separate, and live database writes should be avoided to prevent inconsistencies.
Deep topic analysis must commence with bounded corpus scoring, evidence rows, probability-like ratios, correlations, anomalies, and caveats before engaging LLM interpretation.
New analytics primitives must operate on existing data schemas without introducing new schema changes or external dependencies unless explicitly approved.
Unrestricted data access is forbidden; data-access methods must adhere to governance rules, block Tier X data categories, and be scored by reliability, throughput, cost, errors, and sample count.
Missing optional experiment logs must not impede or mark core governance registry readiness as failed; readiness evaluation should focus on critical, required metrics.
Provider-specific generative model integrations must not hard-code single model IDs but instead dynamically discover or configure candidate models with a 404 fallback mechanism across candidates.
Retries for generative model requests must cease immediately upon encountering authentication or quota-related errors to prevent resource exhaustion and unnecessary API calls.
When parsing multiline strings or indentation-rich layouts, always normalize line-level margins and spaces before collapsing consecutive newline boundaries.
When isolating SQLite databases, maintain logical relationships in application memory/Python mapping rather than relying on attached database files or cross-database joins.
To preserve sequence order in file-backed event logs, mutate loaded lists in-place rather than separating and prepending/appending sub-lists, ensuring chronological integrity.
Avoid using shared or global validation flags directly in loop continuation statements to prevent premature halting of traversal.
Memory OS automation loops must separate snapshot creation, dry-run proposal review, write actions, and scheduler binding to ensure inspectability and approval gating for autonomous operations.
Entitlement-based UI gates must not hide developer or administrative surfaces in local admin mode without an explicit product decision, to ensure operational visibility.
Copy and export features must utilize a single backend formatter to ensure consistent formatting and citation contracts across clipboard actions, file downloads, and automated processes.
Every governed write path requires a nearby read-only audit surface (e.g., a dedicated API endpoint or UI panel) to allow operators to verify records without direct database access.

Safe preview APIs must expose sufficient operational state to verify data ingestion or processing, while actively withholding raw metadata and secret-bearing fields to maintain data security and privacy.
When implementing reciprocal state synchronization across separate frontend components, always include skip-propagation guards to prevent infinite cascade loops.
Avoid nesting absolutely positioned control elements (e.g., close buttons) in deeply nested flex structures if they are intended to align directly with the outer card or component bounds.
Graph dependency routing must resolve package-level scopes using full module paths to prevent over-matching and unintended blast radius to top-level directories.

When deduplicating relational entities, all secondary reference tables (e.g., video_entities, entity_aliases) must be completely updated and foreign-key references handled before deleting redundant canonical entries.
Scoped DOM selectors are preferred over global IDs within widgets to prevent collisions when multiple widget instances are spawned.
When integrating LLM extraction services, the mock flag must be checked before attempting real API key validation to prevent unintended API calls during development or testing.
The Owner retains the full right to override or intervene in any workflow pipeline step where specific expertise is possessed, and these boundaries must be explicitly documented.
Native Python validation checks are preferred for lightweight configuration or inbox contracts to avoid external package overhead while ensuring robust runtime checks.
Explicit, manual dashboard actions are preferred for scheduling checks to avoid CPU and token consumption risks associated with automatic background cron jobs or daemon processes.
implement chat drawer memory OS likes and dislikes and markdown export actions
allow adding custom comments to liked/disliked chat messages

The Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP) using abstract classes and constructor injection must be applied to complex orchestration modules in Python to enable in-memory unit testing, improving speed, stability, and mock cleanliness.
User-facing Memory OS data (user memories) must be injected into system prompts to enrich LLM context, with strict filtering of developer codebase or symbol references to maintain separation.
Employ dependency-free formatters (e.g., for prompt injection) to avoid external packaging overhead and simplify deployment.

Configuration for scheduled background watchers must be validated rigorously, including limits and crawl intervals (e.g., minimum 15 mins), before execution to ensure runtime safety and prevent rate-limit exhaustion.

Batch execution steps for scheduled watchers must be designed to maintain a single transaction connection for all operations (parsing, validation, logging) to avoid database locking issues and ensure atomic operation states.

When refactoring core service modules or extending core APIs, maintain backward-compatible facades and return type signatures to prevent breakage of existing unit test mocks, legacy test consumers, and external integrations.

Data-access methods must be treated as measurable experiments, logging performance and promoted to reusable connectors only upon demonstrated reliability. Insights for promotion and retirement of these methods must be centralized, and operational analytics panels should display clear, ranked method evidence and insights rather than raw experiment logs.

Workflow routing must classify domain and step size before model selection. Routing tools must emit metadata aligned with handoff and capsule validators, and portable installations require workflow manifest validation at bootstrap time to ensure usable routing specifications.

Task capsule metadata and other data structures must be validated as lightweight contracts, ensuring required fields are present while maintaining backward compatibility. Validation rules and corresponding authoring guidelines must be updated synchronously to consistently capture and utilize new metadata.

Roadmap updates for new capabilities should be concrete, defining schemas and utility scripts before execution. The global roadmap must be continuously updated to reflect completed features and capabilities to ensure alignment and coordination across developer and agent workstreams.

Repository-wide best practices, 'gotchas' documents, root onboarding documents, and structural map indexes must be updated dynamically and continuously to reflect new architectural learnings, module additions, or core CLI utilities, preventing future execution regressions.

Analytics scoring layers must be source-agnostic, isolating source-specific logic into adapters to enable reuse of the metric engine across diverse data feeds and tools (CLI, dashboards). When performing combined-source scoring, phrases must be deduplicated per record to prevent inflated counts and ensure accurate metric aggregation.

Proposal classification must precede persistence splits. Metadata validation for lightweight records should occur at the routing layer. Large architecture proposals should be staged with documented override channels for owner expertise. Automating proposal transitions using tests guarantees status updates are code-verified.

When testing locally imported methods, mock the source definition module directly. For modules that execute environment setup or spawn subprocesses during import, critical setup helpers must be mocked as no-ops at the very beginning of the test execution lifecycle to prevent process hijacking or mock path resolution failures.

All data ingestion must enter through a single, governed API surface offering dry-run previews by default. Ingestion of Tier E sources requires explicit allowance and `operator_runtime` privileges. Product ingestion UI workflows must expose preview-first controls that mirror backend persistence semantics, avoiding direct write actions via shortcuts.

Frontend layout persistence mechanisms must implement hard client-side bounds and suppress writes during state restoration. All custom UI widgets must be registered in backend type schemas for proper serialization and layout validation. Layout-relevant keys must be explicitly whitelisted in backend state sanitization filters to prevent unintended removal.

The Global Language Policy must strictly block certain language generation (e.g., Russian) and gate Memory OS responses based on the user's detected language. These language policy instructions, especially gating rules, must be synchronized across all core system prompts and agent rules to ensure consistent enforcement.
